microtheory.name: social_psychology
microtheory.definition: How people's thoughts, feelings, behaviours are influenced by actual, imagined, or implied presence of others (Allport 1954). Major findings: conformity (Asch), obedience (Milgram), bystander effect (Latane + Darley), self-fulfilling prophecy (Merton), in-group/out-group (Tajfel), attribution errors. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate collaborative contexts, how independent substrates influence each other's Mt states.

concepts.name: social_identity_theory
concepts.definition: Tajfel + Turner 1979. People derive self-esteem from group memberships; favour in-group + derogate out-group even on arbitrary categorisations. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity field bias toward concepts within its foundational Mts.

concepts.name: self_categorisation
concepts.definition: Turner et al. 1987. Context determines which identity is salient. Same person identifies as 'mother' at home, 'scientist' at work. Substrate analogue: substrate's currently-active Mt context.

concepts.name: social_comparison
concepts.definition: Festinger 1954. People evaluate themselves by comparison to others. Upward (aspirational), downward (self-protective). Substrate analogue: substrate's assessment cortex compares its own state against peer substrate states (in multi-substrate contexts).

concepts.name: conformity
concepts.definition: Asch 1956. People conform to majority opinion even when they know it's wrong. 75% conformed at least once. Substrate analogue: in collaborative multi-substrate contexts, substrate's Mts gravitating toward majority consensus.

concepts.name: obedience_to_authority
concepts.definition: Milgram 1963. 65% delivered maximal 'electric shocks' to confederates because experimenter said so. Authority overrides moral resistance. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded Rules acting as moral constraints — strong override mechanisms.

concepts.name: social_proof
concepts.definition: Cialdini. When uncertain, people follow what others do. Bandwagon effect. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive ranking of frequently-fired-elsewhere ActionSpecs.

concepts.name: minority_influence
concepts.definition: Moscovici 1969. Consistent minority can convert majority. Substrate analogue: persistent novel concepts that don't align with current Mts can eventually trigger Mt restructuring.

concepts.name: persuasion_dual_process
concepts.definition: Petty + Cacioppo 1986. Elaboration Likelihood Model: central route (deep processing, durable change) vs peripheral route (heuristic cues, brittle change). Substrate analogue: substrate's deep concept integration vs shallow event tagging.

concepts.name: fundamental_attribution_error
concepts.definition: Ross 1977. Over-weight dispositional, under-weight situational causes for others' behaviour. Substrate analogue: substrate's bias toward intrinsic-concept explanations over external context.

concepts.name: actor_observer_bias
concepts.definition: Jones + Nisbett 1972. Attribute own behaviour to situation, others' to disposition. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-introspection vs other-modelling asymmetry.

concepts.name: self_serving_bias
concepts.definition: Successes attributed to self; failures attributed to circumstance. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-protection mechanism for the value-of-self concept.

concepts.name: stereotype
concepts.definition: Cognitive shortcut: schema for a social group. Adaptive when accurate, harmful when wrong + applied to individuals. Allport 1954. Substrate analogue: substrate's category-level Concept activation overriding instance-level information.

concepts.name: prejudice
concepts.definition: Negative affect toward a group based on stereotypes. Substrate analogue: substrate's negative-valence Mt categories that bias evaluation of related concepts.

concepts.name: discrimination
concepts.definition: Behaviour differentially treating individuals based on group membership. Substrate analogue: substrate's differential ActionSpec dispatch based on concept-category.

concepts.name: implicit_bias
concepts.definition: Greenwald + Banaji. Automatic stereotype activation independent of explicit belief. Measured by IAT. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime FilterSpec firing without ArchitectureCortex deliberation.

concepts.name: self_fulfilling_prophecy
concepts.definition: Merton 1948. Expectation about other → treatment → other's behaviour confirms expectation. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-field bias creating self-confirming basin selection.

concepts.name: stereotype_threat
concepts.definition: Steele + Aronson 1995. Awareness of negative stereotype about one's group impairs performance. Substrate analogue: substrate's hyperactive coherence-drive on identity-relevant tasks producing interference.

concepts.name: self_concept_threat
concepts.definition: Information that challenges valued self-views triggers defensive processing. Sherman + Cohen. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen-Mt resistance to disconfirming evidence.

concepts.name: bystander_effect
concepts.definition: Latane + Darley 1968. More bystanders → less likely any one helps. Diffusion of responsibility. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, substrate's drive to act on shared problems weakens with more peers.

concepts.name: social_loafing
concepts.definition: Latane et al. 1979. Individual effort decreases in groups. Substrate analogue: substrate's reduced engagement when handlers redundantly cover a Mt.

concepts.name: group_polarisation
concepts.definition: Moscovici + Zavalloni 1969. Group discussion amplifies pre-existing tendencies. Substrate analogue: substrate's collaborative Mt-alignment producing more-extreme converged states than any individual.

concepts.name: groupthink
concepts.definition: Janis 1972. Cohesive groups suppress dissent → flawed decisions. Bay of Pigs as case. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive overpowering curiosity-drive in aligned-Mt context.

concepts.name: reciprocity_norm
concepts.definition: Cialdini. People feel obligated to return favours. Universal across cultures. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate exchange, balanced give-and-take of Mt content.

concepts.name: fairness_norm
concepts.definition: Equity theory (Adams 1965). People prefer outcomes proportional to inputs; perceive inequality as aversive. Ultimatum game: refusing 'unfair' offers. Substrate analogue: substrate's parsimony-drive sensitive to disproportion.

rules.name: conformity_via_informational_and_normative_influence
rules.head: the substrate is uncertain or motivated to belong
rules.body: it conforms to peers' Mt states — informational influence (peers know better) or normative (be accepted). Asch 1956. Substrate's collaborative alignment mechanism.

rules.name: in_group_favoritism_arises_from_arbitrary_categorisation
rules.head: any meaningful category exists (substrate vs other-substrate)
rules.body: the substrate biases evaluation toward in-group concepts even with no other basis. Tajfel 1971.

rules.name: attribution_bias_overweights_disposition_for_others
rules.head: the substrate explains another agent's behaviour
rules.body: it over-weights stable disposition + under-weights situational context. Ross 1977 fundamental attribution error.

rules.name: self_concept_threat_triggers_defensive_processing
rules.head: evidence appears that challenges the substrate's self_concept
rules.body: the substrate processes it defensively (motivated reasoning, dismissal). Sherman + Cohen. Substrate's identity-protection.

rules.name: bystander_responsibility_diffuses_with_group_size
rules.head: multiple substrates share an observable problem
rules.body: each individual substrate's drive to act on it weakens. Latane + Darley 1968.

rules.name: group_polarisation_amplifies_initial_tendency
rules.head: substrates with aligned Mts interact
rules.body: their post-interaction Mts are more extreme than any pre-interaction state. Moscovici + Zavalloni 1969.
